requirements.raw_text: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units

courses.title: Applied Regression Analysis
courses.requirement: Major Required: 14 units
courses.description: Simple linear regression and scatterplots, multiple linear regression, matrix formulation of regression, least squares estimation, interpretation of regression coefficients, hypothesis tests for regression coefficients, confounding and multicollinearity, interaction and effect modification, regression diagnostics and remedial measures, model selection, use of statistical software packages for all techniques discussed.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; OR C or better in STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140; and C or better in MAT 2240 and MAT 2250 .

courses.title: Mathematical Statistics I
courses.requirement: Major Required: 14 units
courses.description: Theory of probability, discrete and continuous probability distributions, multivariate distributions, distributions of function of random variables, moment generating functions, modes of convergence, asymptotic distributions, central limit theorem.

courses.title: Numerical Analysis I
courses.requirement: Major Required: 14 units
courses.description: Direct and iterative methods to solve linear systems of equations. Matrix splitting, inversions, eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Numerical solutions of non-linear equations. Rates of convergence and techniques to reduce error propagation.

courses.title: Mathematical Modeling I
courses.requirement: Major Required: 14 units
courses.description: Modeling of deterministic systems using ordinary and partial differential equations. Fixed points, bifurcations and stability of solutions. General modeling principles and techniques. Perturbation theory and sensitivity analysis. Case studies.

courses.title: Linear Statistical Models
courses.requirement: Subplan/Option Required: 8-9 units
courses.description: Review of selected linear algebra and probability background material, including projection matrices and the multivariate normal distribution; matrix formulation of the multiple linear regression model, estimation, hypothesis testing, predictions, restrictions, and rank deficiency; one-way, two-way, and higher-way analysis of variance, random effects and variance components; illustration with statistical software and matrix computation software such as R or MATLAB.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C or better in STA 4320 , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Supervised Statistical Consulting
courses.requirement: Subplan/Option Required: 8-9 units
courses.description: Use of computer package and spreadsheet. Statistical and probabilistic modeling techniques. Planning of surveys and experiments. Data analysis, report writing and presentation, oral communication with clients. Role-playing and group discussions. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 4320 or STA 4350 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: May be repeated for a maximum of 4 units of credit

courses.title: Real Analysis I
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Lebesgue measure and integration, Borel sets, monotone functions and functions of bounded variation, L^p spaces, measure spaces and measurable functions, the Radon-Nikodym theorem, the Fubini theorems, applications.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and a C or better MAT 3140 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Nonparametric Statistics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Common nonparametric tests such as sign tests, Wilcoxon test, chisquare test, rank correlation tests and permutation tests. Null distributions of test statistics and their approximations.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 2100 and STA 2260 .

courses.title: Survival Analysis
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Survival models. Types of censoring. Life-tables. Estimation of survival functions from complete and incomplete mortality data. Actuarial and maximum likelihood methods. Kaplan-Meier estimator. Weighted log-rank and Mantel-Haenszel tests. Parametric regression models. Cox proportional hazards model. Probit and Logit models. Use of computer package such as SAS or MINITAB or R.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in the following: STA 2100 and STA 2200 ; STA 2260; or IME 3140.

courses.title: Introduction to Random Processes
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Random walks, Markov chains and processes, transient and recurrent states, stationary and steady state or equilibrium distributions, Chapman-Kolmogorov equation, forward and backward differential equations: Poisson processes, birth-death chains and processes, classical single and multiple server queueing systems, Little’s formula, advanced queueing models.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 2200 and STA 2260 .

courses.title: Applied Data Science and Statistical Learning
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: A comprehensive, hands-on toolkit for modern predictive modeling and data science, with the following core components: data wrangling and cleaning (importing, tidying, merging, and validating real-world datasets); multivariate exploratory data analysis and visualization; core principles of prediction: accuracy metrics, bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting, cross-validation, and out-of-sample evaluation; and modern supervised learning methods for continuous and binary outcomes: linear and logistic regression (including penalized/lasso/ridge/elastic net), discriminant analysis, tree-based models (random forests, gradient boosting), support vector machines, neural networks and deep learning fundamentals. All topics emphasize hands-on implementation in R or Python, rigorous model validation, and clear interpretation of results.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 4320 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Analysis of Variance and Design of Experiments
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: ANOVA techniques, multiple comparisons, computer solutions. Randomized groups and blocks designs, interactions. Latin square, split-plot, simple and confounded factorial designs. Treatment of missing data, incomplete block designs, fractional factorial designs, multifactor experiments with randomization restrictions.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; or C or better in STA 1300 , STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140.

courses.title: Mathematical Statistics II
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Dual Listed as: STA 5411 Methods of point and interval estimation, unbiasedness, mean square error, efficiency, consistency, completeness, sufficient statistics, Neyman-Pearson theory of testing hypotheses, likelihood ratio tests, sequential analysis.

courses.title: Categorical Data Analysis
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Contingency Tables, Odds ratio, Fisher’s exact tests, Chi-square tests, M-tests, Generalized Linear Models including logistic regression and Poisson regression.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 3-4 units
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Time Series Analysis
courses.description: Difference equations. Stationary and non-stationary models. Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions. Autoregressive (AR), Moving average (MA), Autoregressive-moving average (ARMA), and Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models. Models for seasonal time series. Identification, estimation, diagnostic checking and forecasting. Use of computer package such as SAS or MINITAB or R.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in STA 2260 , IME 3140, or STA 2100 and STA 2200 .

courses.title: Random Processes
courses.description: Gaussian processes, covariance matrices, mean and covariance properties, Wiener processes and white noise, second order stationary processes. Analysis of queueing systems with equilibrium results for single and multiple server queues. Almost periodic processes. Frequency distribution of second order stationary processes. Linear filtering. Renewal processes. Method of stages. Priority queues.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing and C or better in STA 4300 , or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Multivariate Data Analysis
courses.description: Multivariate distribution. Variance-covariance matrices. Multivariate Normal distribution,. Inference about a mean vector. Multivariate Regression, MANOVA, Classification and Discriminant analysis, Principal components, Factor analysis and Clustering. Use of computer package such as SAS or R.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing or C or better in STA 2100 , STA 2260 , TOM 3020 , EC 3322 , or IME 3140; and C or better in MAT 2250 .

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Directed Research
courses.requirement: Culminating Experience: 2-4 units
courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.requirement: and
courses.description: Independent research and study under supervision of a faculty advisor. Research results must be reported in an acceptable form. May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 3 units.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.requirement: OR
courses.description: Preparation for the comprehensive examination. Failure to complete exam satisfactorily the second time will result in termination from the program. Not applicable for students in the Mathematics Education emphasis. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.requirement: Summer Sponsored Experience: 0 unit
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
